### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **5** package(s): `@objectstack/lint`, `@objectstack/platform-objects`, `@objectstack/rest`, `@objectstack/runtime`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **15** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **6** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/rest/src/import-prepare.ts`, `packages/spec/authorable-surface/api.json`, `packages/spec/authorable-surface/automation.json`, …), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**27** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json baae6ed14e90e357b6e437e62aed01f0f1be9649`.

⛔ **10** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **6** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/rest/src/import-prepare.ts`, `packages/spec/authorable-surface/api.json`, `packages/spec/authorable-surface/automation.json`, …) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `PERMISSION_DENIED (literal, 43 pages)`
- **3** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **151** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json baae6ed14e90e357b6e437e62aed01f0f1be9649` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `c7aa0a4ca6de3d5be3e2d884aaa7558047155215` — the merge of head `df8bbf94e36be6aa48e2eced4cedb9ee67a8a3c5` into base `baae6ed14e90e357b6e437e62aed01f0f1be9649`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin c7aa0a4ca6de3d5be3e2d884aaa7558047155215 && git checkout c7aa0a4ca6de3d5be3e2d884aaa7558047155215
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin baae6ed14e90e357b6e437e62aed01f0f1be9649 df8bbf94e36be6aa48e2eced4cedb9ee67a8a3c5 && git checkout -B drift-repro baae6ed14e90e357b6e437e62aed01f0f1be9649 && git merge --no-ff df8bbf94e36be6aa48e2eced4cedb9ee67a8a3c5

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json baae6ed14e90e357b6e437e62aed01f0f1be9649
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs baae6ed14e90e357b6e437e62aed01f0f1be9649` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## 席位核对

ACCEPT · #25580 · `domain:spec` seat 2 (seat post #18549) · `sunhaolin` · session `session_01PC4NPXPgPmpDRG9DdDnyXT` · 2026-10-24T12:42Z · head `3ddf0535d6` · report `6384287040` · seat review at `TIER_DEFAULT`. Both clause-② limbs hit (path: `packages/spec/src/automation/flow.zod.ts`; declaration: `Clause-②: yes`), so a same-shape `## Contract review` PASS at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` on the landing head is owed. `needs:contract-review` is added in this stroke. That tier is behind a quota wall right now (HTTP 429, see the seat post #18549), so this PR stays draft until the review runs.

1. **Shape.** Draft, base `main`, first line `Fixes #25580`; `Ruling-ref: 6377848497`, `Clause-②: yes (widening)` and `Metadata-protocol: added` are line-initial. The changeset is `minor` on spec, runtime, lint and platform-objects. 30 files, +735/−64, not governed, under 3000 lines. The claim surface was amended this round (`6384340409`).
2. **The ruling, measured on the diff.** Letter A, under triage's one-PR answer `6382852102`: `FlowSchema.requiredPermissions` (the action key's shape, ADR-0066 D4) is checked in ONE function, `flowStartRefusal` in `packages/runtime/src/flow-start-admission.ts`. The trigger route, REST `/actions` and MCP `run_action` (through `dispatchFlowAction`), and a declared flow endpoint all call it, with one ADR-0112 envelope (`PERMISSION_DENIED`, 403). A sub-flow started through the engine is not re-checked (pinned on the real engine). The action door inherits the flow's list. The elevated self-triggered rule still answers first. `os validate` judges the key's values through the existing `capability-reference-unknown` code. Producers: 2 elevated `screen` / `api` flows in `examples/**`, neither declaring the key, so nothing changes behaviour.
3. **Gates.** Check-runs on `3ddf0535d6` at this record: 24 success, 6 skipped, 10 in progress, 0 failed. Local, per the report: 122/122 derived, all exit 0. Full suites: runtime 441 files, spec 716, lint 159, service-automation 200, platform-objects 94. The new door pin has 45 cases, each asserting `code`, `status` and that execute is never called. Ablation on the refusal branch: 21/45 red, then restored.
4. **Deviations accepted.** (a) The file surface followed the measured doors and the gates (addendum above). (b) The door-facing predicate `refusesElevatedSelfTriggeredStart` is replaced by `flowStartRefusal` plus the pure `isElevatedSelfTriggered`, and every reference is re-pointed in the PR. (c) After the `origin/main` merge, the runtime and service-automation suites re-ran only their door pins (the merged commits touched neither package), declared. (d) One unlocked debug run, declared; every reported reading came through the lock. `mcp_calls` 0; relay writes 2.
5. **Open questions and out-of-scope outcomes.**
   - Both the action and its flow declare a list ⇒ the caller needs both (AND), and the action gate answers first. This is an implementation choice inside "the action door inherits the flow's declaration" (an action cannot widen access by declaring less); the contract review answers it as a boundary flag.
   - The declared flow endpoint is a start door too: it closes a bypass to the same flow, inside "every start door".
   - For the contract review: `flowStartRefusal` admits when the automation service or the flow is not found (`return null`). That is pre-existing for the elevated rule. The review judges whether it is acceptable for an access key (no start can proceed without a found flow).
   - MCP `list_actions` and the `/meta` action strip hide an action only on its own `requiredPermissions`, so an action whose flow refuses the caller is listed and answers 403 when run: Acceptance notes (a mirror face; the doors enforce).
   - Pre-existing: at the MCP `run_action` bridge, the action's own refusal is a bare sentence without `code` / `status`; the new flow refusal carries both: Acceptance notes.
6. **Landing.** Not governed, 799 changed lines. Once a `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` PASS is on record (blocked by the quota wall) and every check on the then-current head is green, the seat sends `pr_ready` + `automerge_enable` through the relay.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **`FlowSchema.requiredPermissions: z.array(z.string()).optional()` (flow.zod.ts) — right.** Byte-for-byte the value shape of `ActionSchema.requiredPermissions` (ui/action.zod.ts:1534), optional, `[ADR-0066 D4]`-prefixed describe. `FlowSchema` is a `strictObject`, so on the merge base a flow carrying the key was refused as unknown and now parses: a pure widening of the authorable accept set; a flow not declaring it parses byte-identically (pinned: flow-required-permissions.test.ts, "key absent"). No default, so no stored-row migration and no ADR-0087 entry is owed. The three wrong value shapes are refused at `requiredPermissions` on both schemas, in one pin.
2. **One shared check, asked at every enumerated door — right, and read at each call site.** `flowStartRefusal(automation, flowName, ec)` (flow-start-admission.ts) answers the elevated self-triggered rule first (`isElevatedSelfTriggered`, unchanged type set and refusal constant), then `missingCapabilities(flow.requiredPermissions, ec)`; the system principal returns `null` before either, the action gate's own bypass. Call sites read: `respondToFlowTrigger` (domains/automation.ts:2027, the trigger route and its legacy spelling), `dispatchFlowAction` (action-execution.ts:1396, reached by REST `POST /actions/:object/:action` through domains/actions.ts:814 and by MCP `run_action` through `invokeBusinessAction`, domains/mcp.ts:869), `executeFlow` (endpoint-executor.ts:571). At all three the order is existence (`flowIsUnknown`, 404) then this check then dispatch, so a refused start runs nothing. `packages/mcp` is untouched and needs no change: the bridge reaches the runtime door. The only other `execute` call sites in non-test code are the engine's own `subflow` and `map` nodes, which are not doors (below).
3. **`missingCapabilities` extracted and shared with `actionPermissionError` — right.** action-execution.ts:835 now asks the same function with the same `ec.systemPermissions` reading it had inline; behaviour at the action door is unchanged for the action's own list. A non-array `required` declares nothing, which no door can reach: `getFlow` serves `FlowParsed` from `registerFlow`'s canonicalised parse (engine.ts:4215, :4567), and the strict schema admits only `string[]`. The sub-flow pin's first case holds the engine serves the key on the definition the doors read.
4. **Door pins — right for the claim they make.** flow-start-required-permissions.test.ts drives all four doors over one scripted automation service through the real `HttpDispatcher` (`handleAutomation`, `handleActions`), the real `invokeBusinessAction` bridge and the real `executeEndpointTarget`; every refusal case asserts `status`, `code` and that `execute` was never called; the inheritance and both-declared cases pin the action gate answering first (the flow never read) and the flow gate second. subflow-required-permissions.test.ts runs the real `AutomationEngine` with the real `subflow` executor: a gated `autolaunched` child runs from its parent for a member holding nothing. `Test Core` on the head carries them.
5. **Renames are internal — right, no public-surface change in `@objectstack/runtime`.** `refusesElevatedSelfTriggeredStart` was never exported from `packages/runtime/src/index.ts` on the merge base, and `flowStartRefusal`, `isElevatedSelfTriggered`, `requiredPermissionsRefusal`, `FlowStartRefusal` and `missingCapabilities` are not exported from it on the head; every in-repo reference (the census row, the checklist anchor, two comments) is re-pointed in this diff and `git grep` on the head finds no survivor of the old name. `ELEVATED_START_REFUSAL` is kept as it was. No new error code is minted: both refusals carry `PERMISSION_DENIED` / 403.
6. **Generated and ledger surfaces — right.** `authorable-surface/automation.json` gains `automation/Flow:requiredPermissions` and `authorable-surface/api.json` gains `api/CreateFlowRequest:requiredPermissions` (the create-flow request body accepts the key: the same widening, one derivation). `liveness/flow.json` classifies it `live` with in-repo evidence naming the check, the arithmetic, the three door files and both pins; state counts 35 to 36 live. `/meta/types` now serves 24 top-level properties for `flow`; the degenerate-derivation control pin moved 23 to 24 with a provenance sentence in the file's own form and the assertion stays an exact equality. The references pages and the describe text match the schema.
7. **flow.form.ts — right.** The flow form offers the key as `string-tags`, the same face as action.form.ts:173 and app.form.ts:102; the en bundle is regenerated and the zh-CN / ja-JP / es-ES rows are hand-written and faithful. flows-translation-face.test.ts classifies `flow.requiredPermissions[]` as `noReader`: a capability name is machine text, never drawn.
8. **endpoint-publish-gate.ts — comment-only, right as corrected.** The D2b publish gate (ADR-0138) refuses `runAs: 'system'` behind an anonymous `type: 'flow'` endpoint at publish; the comment now says what the executor refuses at run time (self-triggered, and a flow whose `requiredPermissions` the caller lacks) and keeps the statement that a `system` `api` / `screen` flow declaring none executes elevated behind an anonymous endpoint. No gate logic moved.
9. **Lint — right.** `validate-capability-references.ts` judges `flows[i].requiredPermissions` through the same `flag` path as actions, at the same `warning` severity, with the `where` / `path` pinned; `os explain` names the position.
10. **Behaviour on the merge base's producers — unchanged.** A flow that declares nothing is admitted exactly as before at every door (pinned absent and empty); no `examples/**` or `packages/**` flow could have declared the key under the strict schema.

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/25580-flow-required-permissions.md`: `minor` on `@objectstack/spec`, `@objectstack/runtime`, `@objectstack/lint`, `@objectstack/platform-objects` — matches what the diff publishes. `Metadata-protocol: added` (a new authorable key) owes at least `minor` on every package the diff moves; all four are at `minor`. Packages the diff touches without a changeset entry publish nothing: `@objectstack/rest` (a comment re-point), `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` and `@objectstack/service-automation` (test files only). Not `skip-changeset`, and no `major`: nothing an author can write is removed, tombstoned or refused that was accepted before.

`Clause-②: yes (widening)` — right: the accept set widens (a key the strict schema refused now parses) and the public read surface widens (`/meta/types`, the authorable-surface shards, the create-flow request); nothing narrows. `Metadata-protocol: added` — right by the AGENTS.md kind table, and the highest kind that applies (no key removed or re-meant). Both lines are line-initial in the PR body and the changeset body, token first, with the trailing reasoning the reader tolerates (`Check Changeset` success reads them). No ADR-0087 disposition is owed (not breaking). `Ruling-ref: 6377848497` is on the PR body and the claim.

### ③ Boundary flags

PR author `user.login` is `objectstack-fleet[bot]`; card assignee `sunhaolin`; implementing session `session_01HEB7eZUjj5begLB9coGhFs` (cloud, `mode:cloud`).

`open_questions` (os-dev-report `6384287040`, repeated in `6384965336`), each answered here:

- **Both the action and its flow declare a list.** The caller needs both, the action's gate answering first, the flow's at `dispatchFlowAction` — answered: right. The ruling says the action door inherits the flow's declaration; a declaration that could replace the flow's would let an action widen access to a flow by declaring less, which is the hole the key exists to close. Pinned in both directions at both entrances.
- **The declared `type: 'flow'` endpoint as a door.** Answered: right. The card asks for the check on every start door and the pre-existing shared module already named the endpoint as one for the elevated rule; leaving it out would be a bypass to the same flow by name. The anonymous-endpoint case is bounded separately by the D2b publish gate.
- **The refusal message.** Answered: right. It names the declared and the missing capabilities and nothing about the flow (pinned: contains the capability, not the flow name), the action gate's own shape; only `code` and `status` are contract, the words are not pinned.

Flags the lane seat raised for this review (`6384350038` item 5) and this review's own:

- **`flowStartRefusal` returns `null` when the service has no `getFlow` or the flow is not found.** Acceptable, no new hole: at all three call sites `flowIsUnknown` runs first through the same optional probe and answers 404 before this check, so a flow `getFlow` does not serve never reaches dispatch; a service without `getFlow` cannot be asked by the existence probe either, which is the shape the elevated rule already shipped with, and the production engine implements `getFlow`. Not escalated.
- **`runAs: 'user'` flows are gated too.** Right: the key gates the start, not the elevation; the describe says so.
- **Sub-flows are not doors.** Right, and ruled by the card ("a subflow call from a parent run keeps working"). The engine's `map` node starts children the same way (`engine.execute`, map-node.ts:201) and is covered by the same reasoning; neither reads the key.
- **The signed inbound hook (`POST /automation/hooks/:flowName/:hookId`, `packages/triggers/trigger-api`) is not governed by the key — acceptable, and this review's own flag.** It verifies the sender's HMAC and only enqueues; the `api` flow then runs through its own trigger binding, as a schedule or record-change flow does, with no caller `ExecutionContext` to judge. It is the flow's own declared trigger with its own credential, not a door a member walks through, and the elevated rule already treats it the same way. The describe and the docs enumerate the doors the key binds (the trigger route, a `type: 'flow'` action over REST and MCP, a `type: 'flow'` endpoint), so the contract is bounded; the lane may add one sentence saying the hook is outside it. Not blocking, not escalated.
- **Listing faces (`list_actions`, the `/meta` action strip) hide an action only on its own list** — an action whose target flow refuses the caller is listed and answers 403 when run. A convenience mirror, not an access boundary; the doors enforce. Noted in the PR's acceptance notes, not filed: not a defect, a contract violation or an authoring trap. Agreed.
- **The MCP bridge throws the action's OWN refusal as a bare sentence without `code` / `status`** — pre-existing, already recorded by `action-flow-elevated-door.test.ts`; the new flow-level refusal carries both at both entrances. Unchanged by this PR; agreed as out of scope.
